label: Preference-independent epistemic reason from actual force and answerability
description: Conditional analyst argument, attribution deferred: take the ordinary belief reason that has force at its subject's actual preference; answerability carries that force to every supplied preference alternative, so it is a preference-independent ordinary reason. Each premise fails in a finite control (goalRelative lacks answerability; forceless lacks the concession). The goal-relative rival grants the concession and denies answerability, so the dispute is isolated in that one bridge. Establishes neither premise.
